title: Practical circuit representations and sources
concepts_taught: Prescribed circuit symbols and connectivity through wires, branches and junctions.
E.m.f. as source energy supplied per unit charge and potential difference as energy transferred per unit charge.
A real source modelled as an e.m.f. in series with internal resistance.
Lost volts and terminal-potential-difference sag while a source supplies current.
representations_used: connected circuit diagrams with component symbols
misconceptions_addressed: Charge is used up when electrical energy is transferred.
E.m.f. and potential difference describe the same energy-transfer role.
The e.m.f. becomes smaller whenever terminal p.d. falls.
skills_students_can_now_use: Recognise and connect prescribed circuit symbols.
Distinguish source energy supply per unit charge from component energy transfer per unit charge.
Use V = E - Ir for a discharging real source.
Find internal resistance from e.m.f., terminal p.d. and current.
next_module_can_assume: Circuit branches and junctions can be identified from connectivity.
A real source has e.m.f. E, internal resistance r and terminal p.d. V = E - Ir while discharging.
Charge remains conserved while electrical energy is transferred.
next_module_must_not_assume: Kirchhoff's first law at a junction.
Kirchhoff's second law as a general loop method.
